How I feel as a console gamer who frequently posts in /v/PCGaming

I have an Xbox One. I have a Wii U also - but I rarely touch that - and a 3DS that I play more often. I used to be a PC Gamer, but I haven't been for about ten years since PC is mostly digital now; living in rural Alaska means putting up with a low bandwidth cap, so having everything on physical discs makes that a bit easier.

I try to post frequently in /v/PCGaming and the rest of Voat's numerous gaming subs because I'd like to see them grow. The thing I like about Voat's gaming communities is that for the most part people are just happy to coexist and share the same interest in gaming.

I'm the opposite!

Always been a console gamer, last gen saw me move to a PC.

What did it was the more and more games coming out with controller support, and Valve's recognising PC couch co-op gaming.

I still plan on hopping back into the new console generation's scene soon. With PS4K announced, soon a PS4 won't be tooo expensive!

Destiny looks pretty damn good.

Oh man, I completely agree with you there. It's nothing short of inspiring how many inroads PC gaming has made for the living room, for mainstream AAA releases, and for Linux support. The indie scene was already great, but even that is growing at an impressive rate.

1. 4K res on ANY of the current consoles is going to suck massive balls (unless it's video only and even then I bet performance won't be good)

  2. Destiny is huge disappointment compared to what Bungie tried to say it would be. Huge.

I don't care about resolution, I said I'm happy about the PS4K b/c of the price drop it will bring!

A lot of people like Destiny! No one thinks it's amazing in one area; but it excels in enough areas to have replayability. Plus, Bungie's going to keep adding content for 10 years? That's awesomeeee.

I agree; my only qualm with Destiny is that I ran out of content too quickly, but that was before the Taken King expansion. It could be that they've improved it and I just haven't been back to it to check. The only other qualm I had is that making it an MMO (or at least having strangers forced into your game) seems completely unnecessary to me.

Things I did enjoy about Destiny is the gameplay, especially in terms of co-op. I love games that let me play through the main game as a squad of different classes, and to have that ability in a FPS game is great. I'm not interested in going back to Destiny because I feel like the ship has sailed for me and I'm caught up with so many other great games, but I do want to acknowledge the things that it did right along with the things that it didn't.

To be fair, I've barely played it and don't own it. I'm completely speaking off of reviews I've read.

The thing that has always gotten me to purchase a console in the past (besides a cpl price drops) is one big game. I suppose none of the systems new games have done it for me, yet. Destiny's no exception, but when I say this to my friend's with new gen consoles- they all say Destiny's that game. But you're making me more skeptical of it haha.

What's the good game that should buy me over, in your opinion. Or is there some hopefuls on the horizon? I've seen good things being said about PSN/XBL shop games.

I think if you've got buddies that enjoy Destiny than you'd have fun playing with them. I got out of Destiny before the Taken King and that's supposed to add a lot in itself, not to mention any future content. It's not a game that I'd enjoy playing single-player, but for co-op campaign it's pretty fun :)

Everything else I play I'm pretty sure has PC and PS4 versions: Rocket League, Rainbow Six: Siege, The Division.

Really I don't think exclusives could sell a console for me, but having a few close friends on a specific platform absolutely could.
